name: Oracle Open Agent Specification (Agent Spec)
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Stable release exists; language and development versions differ
hdp_coverage: Agent/flow topology; LLM and provider configuration; tools; MCP/A2A components; typed I/O; serialization; sensitive fields; runtime adapters
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Does not cover the full purpose-to-outcome requirements model, evaluator custody, assurance claims, evidence integrity/retention, risk acceptance, operational invalidation, or HDP package resolution
fit_for_hdp: High as an optional executable agent/flow profile; low as the HDP root model
recommended_adoption: Define a versioned Agent Spec adapter/profile and preserve exported Agent Spec as a generated artifact with source and output digests; do not make it the canonical HDP document
key_risks: Version drift between SDK, language payload, and development docs; adapter behavior can reduce portability; extensibility may hide runtime-specific semantics

name: Oracle create-agent-spec skill
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Released authoring skill in the Oracle repository; not normative language text
hdp_coverage: Intent parsing; Agent-versus-Flow choice; SDK construction/export; MCP/tool selection; input/output contracts; secret handling; side-effect confirmation; validation
material_omissions_or_non_fit: No stable skill-spec version of its own; no HDP requirements, evaluator, assurance, traceability, or package semantics; relies on Python SDK availability
fit_for_hdp: High for an adapter-generation skill; not suitable as a conformance source
recommended_adoption: Reuse its build-through-SDK, no-handwritten-serialization, round-trip validation, secret exclusion, and confirmation patterns in the HDP Agent Spec generator; cite it as guidance only
key_risks: Skill behavior can change with repository releases; generator availability and runtime adapters remain prerequisites

name: Agent Spec Eval
hdp_coverage: Datasets; samples; deterministic and LLM metrics; evaluator orchestration; retries; repetition/ensembles; result details; concurrency; sensitive evaluation data
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Does not by itself enforce an evaluator trust boundary, hidden-fixture custody, system-under-test execution, side-effect state verification, business-outcome traceability, assurance claim issuance, or evidence integrity
recommended_adoption: Map HDP public datasets/metrics/result schemas to Agent Spec Eval where useful, but keep the HDP evaluator external, independently versioned, and authoritative; Agent Spec Eval output is evidence input, not final acceptance by definition
key_risks: LLM-judge non-determinism; evaluator leakage if used inside the harness; retries can hide instability; result details may contain sensitive data

name: Agent Spec Tracing
current_version_or_revision: Included in stable PyAgentSpec 26.1.2; development docs continue evolving
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Released extension with standard event/span semantics
hdp_coverage: LLM, tool, agent, flow, node, state, exception, confirmation, and human-in-loop spans/events; correlation identifiers; sensitive-field marking; processor interface
material_omissions_or_non_fit: No canonical evidence ledger, artifact digest/attestation, retention/custody, sampling completeness proof, policy-decision model, business outcome, or assurance graph
fit_for_hdp: High as an observability vocabulary adapter
recommended_adoption: Use as one accepted trace input vocabulary and define a lossless mapping to HDP observations/evidence; add HDP provenance, integrity, retention, audience, completeness, and claim links outside the trace model
key_risks: Trace payloads can expose prompts, tool I/O, state, and errors; asynchronous exporters may drop events; event presence does not prove completeness or correctness

name: JSON Schema
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current published version; newer snapshot work is not a released draft
hdp_coverage: Canonical structural grammar; typed objects and arrays; references; composition; annotations; conditional constraints; vocabularies; meta-schema validation
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Cannot enforce most cross-document reference, semantic, implementation, outcome, temporal, authorization, or assurance rules
fit_for_hdp: Very high for HDP structural validation
recommended_adoption: Make Draft 2020-12 the normative structural layer; pin $schema and $id; keep L2+ semantic checks and evaluator gates separate; ship conformance fixtures and validate the schema against its meta-schema
key_risks: Validator feature variance; ambiguous format assertion unless vocabulary behavior is explicit; remote reference fetching creates supply-chain and availability risk

name: Agent Skills
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Open, cross-product format; no tags or releases observed
hdp_coverage: Portable procedural knowledge; SKILL.md discovery and activation; progressive disclosure; optional scripts, references, and assets
material_omissions_or_non_fit: No normative input/output schema, dependency lock, execution isolation, permission enforcement, artifact provenance, evaluator boundary, conformance version, or assurance model
fit_for_hdp: High for packaging the HDP analysis/authoring skill; low for the HDP definition itself
recommended_adoption: Publish a separate HDP analysis/generation skill that follows Agent Skills, pins its own package version and dependencies, validates its outputs, and treats allowed-tools as advisory unless the host enforces them
key_risks: Living-spec drift; instruction injection and executable script risk; client support differs; experimental allowed-tools is not a security boundary

name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Released current protocol revision; modern stateless core introduces breaking changes from 2025-11-25
hdp_coverage: Tool, resource, and prompt discovery/invocation; client/server capability discovery; transports; authorization; elicitation/MRTR; structured schemas; extensions
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Does not define harness intent, internal orchestration, model behavior, evaluator independence, outcome measures, assurance claims, tool semantic safety, or business authorization policy
recommended_adoption: Represent MCP as an explicit tool/resource protocol binding with pinned revision and capability expectations; validate schemas and auth metadata; keep HDP permissions, approval, data, retry, idempotency, and evidence policies authoritative
key_risks: Major migration from stateful legacy era; authorization complexity; tool descriptions are untrusted input; server capability/runtime drift; deprecated roots/sampling/logging

name: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
current_version_or_revision: Repository release 1.0.1; negotiated protocol 1.0; published page labels 1.0.0
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Stable 1.0 protocol family; patch is ignored for protocol compatibility
hdp_coverage: Agent discovery and signed Agent Cards; agent interfaces; tasks, messages, parts, artifacts; streaming/polling/push; multi-tenancy; version negotiation; security schemes
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Does not define internal multi-agent orchestration, shared memory consistency, delegation authority, business acceptance, evaluator custody, evidence integrity, or end-to-end assurance
fit_for_hdp: High for external agent-to-agent interfaces; low for internal harness topology
recommended_adoption: Use A2A only where a role crosses a process, trust, vendor, or organizational boundary; pin implementation release and declare negotiated 1.0 compatibility; bind Agent Card claims to separately verified HDP capability/evidence records
key_risks: Agent Card claims may be stale or self-asserted; 0.3-to-1.0 wire break; a signature proves bytes against a key but trust still depends on key binding and does not prove capability; remote delegation expands authorization and data boundaries

name: OpenAPI Specification
hdp_coverage: Language-agnostic HTTP API operations, inputs/outputs, security schemes, servers, callbacks/webhooks, streaming media, reusable schemas, extension points
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Does not specify implementation behavior, authorization decisions, side-effect safety, runtime availability, evaluator logic, or assurance evidence; its informational schema is not the normative text
recommended_adoption: Allow version-pinned OpenAPI 3.2.0 contracts by reference and digest; extract operation IDs and schemas into semantic checks; require validator/toolchain capability declaration and never treat schema validation as behavioral proof
key_risks: 3.2 tooling support may lag; specification extensions can become opaque; remote references and Markdown require sanitization; schema cycles can exhaust parsers

name: Open Agentic Schema Framework (OASF)
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Active release; some official guide examples still use schema 1.0.0 and Draft-07
hdp_coverage: Agent record metadata; skill/domain taxonomies; modules; locators; discovery; versioned records; validation and translation services
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Focuses on discovery and declared capabilities, not executable harness behavior, requirements/outcomes, evaluator separation, permission enforcement, evidence strength, or assurance validity; schema dialect differs from HDP
recommended_adoption: Provide an optional OASF 1.1.x export/profile for HDP identity, capabilities, modules, and locators; retain HDP URIs/digests and verification state; never convert self-declared OASF skills into assurance claims
key_risks: Taxonomy and release drift; guide/release mismatch; Draft-07 versus HDP Draft 2020-12; validation API and generated schema differ in coverage; discovery claims can be mistaken for verified capability

name: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current published standard, stage 90.92, with replacement committee draft under development
hdp_coverage: Requirements-engineering life-cycle processes; required information items; contents and format guidance; stakeholder/system/software requirements context
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Public catalog abstract is insufficient for clause-level conformance mapping; not agent- or harness-specific; does not provide serialization, runtime, evaluation protocol, or evidence store
fit_for_hdp: High as requirements-process and information-quality authority
recommended_adoption: Crosswalk HDP requirement, assumption, interface, verification, and traceability fields to the licensed standard during formalization; use the public abstract only for design direction and do not claim conformance yet
key_risks: Revision is underway; full normative text is licensed; premature conformance claims would be unsupported

name: NIST AI RMF 1.0, GAI Profile, and TEVV resources
current_version_or_revision: AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1); GAI Profile NIST AI 600-1
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current published voluntary framework/profile; AI RMF 1.0 is being revised
hdp_coverage: Govern/Map/Measure/Manage risk cycle; socio-technical context; trustworthy characteristics; life-cycle TEVV; GAI governance, provenance, pre-deployment testing, and incident disclosure
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Not a conformance standard or machine schema; does not prescribe an HDP package, agent protocol, assurance metamodel, or universal metric thresholds
fit_for_hdp: Very high for risk, evaluation, monitoring, and governance semantics
recommended_adoption: Create a non-normative crosswalk from HDP risks, requirements, measures, evaluation, monitoring, incidents, and claims to AI RMF outcomes and GAI actions; require explicit tailoring and never label a package NIST-compliant solely from the crosswalk
key_risks: Framework revision may change labels; checklist use can defeat risk-based tailoring; TEVV remains context-specific and cannot be reduced to one score

name: OMG Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM)
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest formal version listed by OMG with normative PDF and XML
hdp_coverage: Structured claims, arguments, evidence/artifacts, terminology, citations, assurance-case packages, and machine-readable exchange
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Large metamodel and tooling burden; not harness-specific; does not define runtime traces, agent protocols, AI metrics, evidence collection, or evaluator custody by itself
fit_for_hdp: High conceptual fit for HDP assurance and traceability; medium implementation fit for v0.1
recommended_adoption: Model HDP claims/evidence/trace edges so a lossless or explicitly qualified SACM export remains possible; defer full SACM serialization until real assurance exchange requires it
key_risks: Over-modeling can make v0.1 unusable; a partial mapping can falsely imply SACM conformance; evidence credibility still requires HDP provenance and custody rules

name: Natural-Language Agent Harnesses
hdp_coverage: Editable natural-language run policy; shared runtime interpretation; handoffs; state updates; validation gates; artifact contracts; portability and ablation of harness policy
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Natural language is ambiguous and runtime interpretation is model-dependent; does not supply a consensus schema, formal conformance, external evaluator custody, permissions, or assurance evidence model
fit_for_hdp: High as a design experiment and human-readable policy layer; low as the normative HDP execution contract
recommended_adoption: Permit natural-language policy as reviewed explanatory content linked to typed requirements and controls; require machine-enforced permissions, budgets, schemas, and acceptance rules to remain authoritative
key_risks: Policy/runtime semantic drift; prompt injection; non-deterministic interpretation; portability claims are benchmark-bounded; treating prose as enforcement would weaken controls

name: AI harness engineering research landscape
current_version_or_revision: AHE arXiv v4; Code as Agent Harness v1; From Prompts to Contracts v1; Model or Harness v1
status_as_of_2026_08_12: Rapidly evolving 2026 preprint literature; no consensus standard
hdp_coverage: Model/harness separation; code-owned guarantees; component, experience, and decision observability; falsifiable edits; artifact-backed validation; model substitution; failure localization across system interactions
material_omissions_or_non_fit: Benchmark and implementation specific; peer review often absent; taxonomies and measured gains are not normative; autonomous self-evolution creates governance and regression hazards
fit_for_hdp: Very high as rationale and experiment design input; not a conformance authority
recommended_adoption: Adopt testable contracts, explicit component inventory, versioned observations, fault injection, model-substitution tests, and repair ownership; gate any harness evolution through independent evaluation, rollback, scope, and approval rules
key_risks: Benchmark overfitting; hidden confounders between model and harness; automatic edits can expand permissions or regress unmeasured behavior; research claims may change with new versions
